# Jurisdiction reference: North Carolina (statewide)

Optional reference. Use it only when the matter profile names North Carolina as the jurisdiction. County- and court-specific items belong in the matter's court profile (`../court-profile-template.md`), not here.

Statewide sources checked 2026-09-30 by the kit review. Re-check before each filing; rules and statutes change. "Verified" means the text was read at the primary source on the date shown. It is not a citator check, and it is not a conclusion that the provision governs a particular filing.

## Worked example for K4 (current law)

N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-1415 was amended by S.L. 2025-70 and S.L. 2025-93 (https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-1415.html, checked 2026-09-30). Check the history note of every section for amendments like these before relying on it.

## North Carolina values used by the generic checklist

| Checklist item | North Carolina source |
|---|---|
| B1 primary sources | Statutes: ncleg.gov. Court rules: nccourts.gov. |
| D2 paper format | General Rules of Practice Rule 5 / 5.1 (letter size, unfolded, firmly bound, no manuscript cover; cover sheet in civil actions, special proceedings, and estates). |
| D3 sensitive information | General Rules of Practice Rule 5(e). |
| D4 local rules | The county's page under https://www.nccourts.gov/locations/ (local rules and forms). |
| D5 time computation | N.C. R. Civ. P. 6(a); criminal pretrial motion timing N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 15A-952 and 15A-976 (verify for the motion type). |
| D6 signature and verification | N.C. R. Civ. P. 11 for civil papers; N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-977(a) affidavit for a superior court suppression motion. |
| K11 evidence | North Carolina Rules of Evidence, N.C. Gen. Stat. § 8C-1. |

## Appellate preservation and superior-court plea procedure (checked 2026-10-10)

The following additions are candidate authorities. The accompanying [authority ledger](north-carolina-authority-ledger.json) records the official source, proposition, pincite, publication status, applicability limits, treatment status, and verification date. Reading governing text does not complete current-treatment or matter-specific review. The authority ledger for the matter must approve reliance under K1 and K4 before a substantive assertion is used in a matter document.

| Provision | Checked proposition and limits |
|---|---|
| [N.C. R. App. P. 4(a)-(c)](https://www.nccourts.gov/assets/inline-files/North%20Carolina%20Rules%20of%20Appellate%20Procedure%20-%20Codified%202%20September%202025_2.pdf?VersionId=6VEOilo_YHmi6ZuBBZSwTOos_5q.Okf4) (Printed p. 18) | Criminal appellate notice: oral notice at trial, or written notice filed and served within fourteen days of judgment or a qualifying timely MAR ruling. District-to-superior appeals use separate statutes. |
| [N.C. R. App. P. 10(a)(1)-(4)](https://www.nccourts.gov/assets/inline-files/North%20Carolina%20Rules%20of%20Appellate%20Procedure%20-%20Codified%202%20September%202025_2.pdf?VersionId=6VEOilo_YHmi6ZuBBZSwTOos_5q.Okf4) (Printed pp. 31-33) | Preservation ordinarily requires a timely specific request and ruling. Jury-instruction objections precede deliberation when opportunity exists. A dismissal motion at the close of all evidence preserves sufficiency regardless of an earlier motion; introducing defense evidence waives denial of the State-close motion. Plain error must be distinctly asserted; its availability requires separate precedent review. |
| [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-1444(a), (a1), (a2), (e)](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-1444.html) (Subsections (a), (a1), (a2), (e)) | Guilty-plea appellate rights are limited, with exceptions including specified sentencing issues, section 15A-979, and denial of plea withdrawal. Subsection (a1) concerns evidentiary support for a nonpresumptive felony minimum; (a2) identifies sentencing legality issues. Certiorari is a separate route, not an automatic appeal. |
| [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-979(b)](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-979.html) (Subsection (b)) | A final suppression denial may be reviewed on appeal from conviction, including conviction on a guilty plea. Reservation, notice, waiver, and other procedural requirements need current primary-opinion review. |
| [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-1021](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-1021.html) (Subsections (a)-(c)) | Superior-court plea discussions may involve charge or sentence concessions and judicial participation. Improper pressure is prohibited. A judge may withdraw advance concurrence when later information is inconsistent with the arrangement. |
| [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-1022](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-1022.html) (Subsections (a)-(d)) | Plea acceptance requires the statutory rights inquiry, informed choice, and factual basis. Personal-address requirements have statutory exceptions for corporations and qualifying misdemeanor appearance waivers. A no-contest plea does not require an admission of guilt. |
| [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 15A-1023](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_15A/GS_15A-1023.html) (Subsections (a)-(c)) | Sentence arrangements must be disclosed. Rejection requires reasons, releases the parties from the agreement, and permits modification and the prescribed continuance; rejection is recorded on the plea transcript. Charge-only arrangements also must be disclosed. |

### Standards-of-review research locator

The [Court of Appeals Legal Standards Database](https://www.nccourts.gov/courts/court-of-appeals/legal-standards-database) is a secondary compilation, not a controlling opinion. Its [PDF](https://www.nccourts.gov/assets/inline-files/NC%20Legal%20Standards.pdf) states a revision date of 26 July 2016. The host warns that it is illustrative and requires independent research and citation checking. Later law has not been checked for these entries; substantive standards remain UNVERIFIED.

| Research topic | Printed pages |
|---|---|
| Criminal pretrial issues | 28 |
| Pleas, discovery sanctions, preservation | 29 |
| Plain error and dismissal motions | 30 |
| Jury instructions | 31-32 |
| Closing argument and sentencing | 33 |
| Postconviction issues | 34 |
| Probation | 35 |

Each topic requires retrieval of the actual opinion, confirmation of the exact holding and pincite, assessment of binding status and subsequent treatment, and a matter-ledger entry. The compilation's date or court hosting does not satisfy those steps. Civil settlement procedure is outside the plea-procedure additions and remains unverified.

## Not verified (do not state as rule until checked)

- Font, margin, line-spacing, and page-limit requirements for any particular county or court (check the court profile and local rules).
- The content of any county's local case management or docketing plans (record them in the court profile).
- Whether North Carolina state courts apply the federal *Twombly*/*Iqbal* plausibility standard to N.C. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6) motions.
- Whether North Carolina requires parallel citations in trial-court filings.
- Signature and verification requirements specific to criminal motions filed by an unrepresented defendant.
- The effective-date and applicability provisions of S.L. 2025-70 and S.L. 2025-93 for any given case.
